Subject: Renewal mechanics + question on termination for convenience (MSA redline)

Hi Marissa / Markus,

Thanks for sending the MSA — attached is our procurement redline (Nimbus_MSA_v1_redline.docx). A couple of items we need clarity on before legal will sign:

- Auto-renew: we typically ask for 60 days notice for non-renewal; your MSA shows 90 days. Is there flexibility to reduce to 60 days for enterprise pilots?
- Termination for convenience (TFC): we want a short wind-down (30 days) and pro-rated refund for unused committed volume. Your team redlined out refunds entirely.
- Order form sync: we need the renewal cadence to align between MSA and Order Form (especially pricing triggers).

Can we schedule a quick 30-min call today or tomorrow to walk through these? We prefer to have procurement and finance on the line.

Attachments: Nimbus_MSA_v1_redline.docx (track changes)

Thanks,
Elena
Procurement Lead
Nimbus Health Co.

Subject: Re: Renewal mechanics + question on termination for convenience (MSA redline)

Hi Elena — thanks for the redline and clear notes. We're happy to get this across the finish line. Quick summary from Sales ops perspective and a proposed plan:

- Auto-renew notice: We can agree to move from 90 -> 60 days for pilot / single-year commitments, provided pricing remains the same during the renewal window. For multi-year deals we prefer 90 days.
- TFC refund: We typically offer pro-rated refunds for prepaid committed spend, but we ask for a short wind-down (30 days) to return data and hand off.
- Order form alignment: we'll push an updated Order Form that references the MSA renewal cadence explicitly and calls out price-change notice triggers.

Karthik and Laura — can you review the above two compromise points and confirm legal and billing are comfortable? If yes, I'll send an updated bundle (RNW_internal_comments.pdf + revised OrderForm) and propose a 30-min call this afternoon at 3pm PT.

Elena — if 3pm PT works, I'll calendar invite and include our finance lead (Ben) for invoice questions.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Renewal mechanics + question on termination for convenience (MSA redline)

Marissa / Elena — I reviewed the redline and Marissa's suggested compromise. A few legal notes and a proposed clause (high level):

1) Auto-renew / notice window
- Compromise: For pilots and single-year agreements, Redwood accepts 60-day notice to opt out. For multi-year or committed capacity agreements, maintain 90-day notice.
- We'll add a cross-reference in Order Form Section 2 (Term) that explicitly overrides MSA notice where the Order Form specifies a shorter window.

2) Termination for convenience (TFC)
- We'll accept TFC with a 30-day wind-down and pro-rata refund of prepaid amounts for unused committed spend, provided: (a) customer returns data and removes access; (b) any third-party pass-through costs are paid; (c) Redwood retains right to preserve logs for audit for 90 days.
- Proposed MSA text snippet to add (for legal to negotiate):
  "If Customer terminates for convenience, Redwood shall provide a thirty (30) day transition period during which Customer shall continue to have access to Services. Customer will receive a pro-rated refund for any pre-paid, unused committed fees, net of any third-party costs reasonably incurred by Redwood. Redwood will retain service logs for 90 days for audit and transition purposes."

3) Pricing-change notice
- We will add a clause requiring Redwood to provide 45 days' prior written notice for any material price change and allow customers to decline renewal if price increases exceed a defined threshold (e.g., 10%). This helps procurement approve auto-renew changes.

If those three items are acceptable, I can prepare tracked-change language and send back. Also — for execution, we recommend the Order Form include a checkbox to indicate whether a specific Order Form is subject to pilot notice exception. That avoids ambiguity later.

Markus / Elena — thoughts?

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

Thanks Karthik — that text is clear and mostly acceptable. A couple of small asks from our side:

- Pilot carveout: for pilot accounts < $100k we need a standard 60-day notice and the ability to opt-out automatically without procurement escalation. Can you confirm the Order Form checkbox approach will be operationalized in our HubSpot/renewal flows?
- Refund timing: will pro-rated refunds be issued within 45 days of termination? We want a firm timetable for finance.

If you can confirm those two items in writing, procurement will sign off. We're available 3pm PT today for a quick alignment if you'd like to finalize live.

Best,
Elena

Elena — confirmed and thank you. Quick bullets and next steps so all teams have one source of truth:

- Pilot carveout: Order Form will include a "Pilot Notice = 60 days" checkbox; our sales ops team will mark this at signature for deals < $100k. HubSpot property will be updated to populate renewal cadence for downstream billing. (Laura — I'll need your help to add the property and automation.)
- Refund timing: Redwood agrees to issue pro-rated refunds within 45 days after effective termination, net of any third-party pass-through costs. Finance will include this in the Order Form payment terms. (Ben — please confirm you can operationalize.)
- MSA language: Karthik will send tracked changes to the MSA that reflect the TFC paragraph and the pricing-change notice (45 days prior notice and 10% threshold for opt-out).
- Docs attached: RNW_internal_comments.pdf (internal comment set) and a draft revised OrderForm_Nimbus_20270506.pdf. I'll send a DocuSign envelope once legal signs off.

Proposed 30-min call at 3:00pm PT today to finalize; sending calendar now.

Thanks everyone — feels like we're close.

Best,
Marissa
